resources.string: Dereel uses this access to recognise Reels, Shorts and Spotlight screens in the Instagram, YouTube, Facebook Lite and Snapchat apps, and to go back or cover them when they’re blocked. It’s set up to receive events from those four apps only. Processing happens on this phone. Dereel doesn’t save or send messages, screenshots or what you watch.

To block short videos inside the Instagram, YouTube, Facebook Lite and Snapchat apps, Dereel needs Android Accessibility access.
Accessibility access is powerful. It lets Dereel see what’s on screen in Instagram, YouTube, Facebook Lite and Snapchat, which can include messages and other personal content.

Dereel checks which app is in front and the screen’s layout identifiers, to recognise a Reels, Shorts or Spotlight screen. It’s set up to receive events from Instagram, YouTube, Facebook Lite and Snapchat only.
Processing happens on this phone. Dereel doesn’t save or send messages, screenshots or what you watch. It keeps only the time spent on those short-video screens, on this phone, for 30 days.
When a blocked screen opens, Dereel goes back once or covers it, and tells you why.
You can turn this off at any time in Android Settings. Your other Dereel features keep working without it.
If Android says this setting is restricted, open Dereel’s App info, tap the menu and choose “Allow restricted settings”.

Supported versions, known gaps and how Dereel handles your data.
Open source. No account, no analytics and no ads. Your settings and history stay on this phone.
Instagram, Facebook, YouTube and Snapchat, and their logos, are trademarks of their owners. Dereel isn’t affiliated with or endorsed by them.
These apps and websites change often. This is what Dereel covers in this version, and where it may not work.
Not yet verified on a device for this release.
Reels are recognised in the full-screen Reels viewer and the Reels tab. Reels playing inside your home feed aren’t blocked.
Reels sent to you in Messages follow your usual rules in the app. Open Instagram inside Dereel to watch one.
Shorts are recognised in the Shorts player. Shorts shelves on the home screen aren’t hidden in the app.
Recommendations and ads aren’t filtered in the app.
Recognition depends on the app’s layout and may stop working after an update. If Dereel can’t recognise the layout, Home shows Needs attention.
The Reels tab and reel pages are blocked, including after in-page navigation, refresh, Back and Forward. Reels in your home feed aren’t blocked.
Explore, suggested and sponsored filters depend on Instagram’s page layout and English labels. Not every ad is removed.
Shorts pages are blocked and Shorts shelves are hidden. A Short opened as a regular video link isn’t recognised as a Short.
Google may refuse to sign in inside Dereel’s browser. Browsing and search still work without signing in.
Promoted-item filtering is best effort. Ads in the video player aren’t removed.

Reel pages, the Reels feed, reel share links and the Video tab are blocked, including after in-page navigation, refresh, Back and Forward. A reel that plays inside your feed without opening its own page isn’t blocked.
Hiding the Reels and Video shortcuts depends on Facebook’s page layout. If a shortcut still shows, opening it is blocked.
Facebook’s mobile website may ask you to use the Messenger app for messages. Dereel doesn’t open other apps for you.
Reels are recognised by Facebook Lite’s full-screen video player. Any other video opened full screen there is blocked too. Videos that play inside the feed aren’t blocked.
The regular Facebook app isn’t supported. Reels there aren’t blocked.
Spotlight is recognised when its full-screen feed is open. Chats, the camera and the map aren’t affected.
Videos in Stories and Discover aren’t blocked.
Snapchat can’t be opened inside Dereel, so there are no extra filters for it.
One account at a time inside Dereel.
Dereel is a voluntary self-control tool. It can’t prevent uninstalling, turning off access, modified devices or every change these apps and websites make.

If an app keeps a short video playing in a small floating window after you leave it (picture-in-picture), Dereel doesn’t see it: that time isn’t counted or limited. You can turn off picture-in-picture for the app in Android settings.
The “protection has stopped” alert can’t be shown if Android stops Dereel completely. Home always shows the real state when you open it.
No Dereel account, analytics, advertising code or automatic uploads.
Stored on this phone: your settings, temporary access, and time spent on short-video screens for 30 days.
Never stored by Dereel: messages, page text, screenshots, browsing history, passwords or account names.
Accessibility processing happens on this phone, for Instagram, YouTube, Facebook Lite and Snapchat only.
Dereel’s data isn’t included in Android backups.
